# Spec: Auto-generated Employee Portal Account

Status: APPROVED by John 2026-11-02. Plan: tasks/plan-employee-portal-account.md. Note: PHP here has no sodium, so the encrypted copy uses openssl AES-256-GCM (see plan). No code written.
Author: Claude, 2026-11-02. Skill: agent-skills:spec-driven-development.

## Objective
Today HR creates an employee, then a Super Admin separately creates a user (Users & Access > Create New User) and links it (Create Employee > "User account: Link later"). Two steps, two people, easy to forget.

Change: **creating an employee automatically creates their portal account** with a generated password. HR can see the password from Users & Access (eye icon). The employee may change it. If an employee forgets it, they file a ticket to HR.

Users: HR (creates employees, hands out credentials), Super Admin (user management), Employee (logs in, changes password).

### Requirements (from John, 2026-11-02)
1. Create Employee auto-creates a user (role Employee, linked to the new employee row). Remove the "User account / Link later" field (index.php ~1319, ~1640).
2. Remove the "Create New User" form on Users & Access (index.php ~1785, action `create_user`). Non-employee accounts (HR, Admin, Client) need a path, see Q3.
3. Password is generated by the system, not typed.
4. Employee can change their own password.
5. HR can still see the password in the Users table via the eye icon (today the eye only shows a value right after a reset, `password_reset_reveal`).
6. Forgotten password: employee raises a ticket; HR handles it (new ticket type / category, then HR resets and hands over the new password).

## Decisions from John (2026-11-02, round 1)
- D1 **Account email is automatic and locked**: `firstnamelastname@<company domain>`. Not editable by HR or the employee.
- D2 The account is created the moment the employee record is created and shows at once in Users & Access (User Accounts list).
- D3 Remove the Create New User form. Existing accounts not linked to an employee (the Super Administrator row John circled, HR/Recruiter/Payroll accounts) stay exactly as they are.
- D4 **HR can view the password anytime, no day limit, even after the employee changed it.** John asked what to store; see "Password storage".
- D5 Forgotten password: employee files it under the existing **HR Requests (employee side)** in ticketing, not a new module.
- D6 Open Question answers: duplicate names get a number (`juandelacruz2@pmbsi.com`); ticket goes to the HR queue under category "Portal account / forgotten password".
- D7 **Role is chosen on Create Employee > Employment information** (new "Role" field). For now only two choices: **HR** and **Employee**. The auto account gets that role. An employee who is also HR (e.g. introduced to HRIS for training) is simply created with role HR. More roles can be added to the dropdown later; the existing Change role action still works.
- D8 **Every HR user may use the eye icon**, not only Super Admin, so HR needs access to a Users & Access view (read-only for HR). Exact scope: Q1.
- D9 Existing employees without a login account: out of scope for this patch (nothing automatic, no button). Existing accounts untouched.
- D10 **Email domain follows the Company field** (Employment information, already required): PMBSI -> `juandelacruz@pmbsi.com`, 2LOG -> `juandelacruz@2log.com`. Companies added later get their own domain. Today company is a fixed list `[2LOG, PMBSI]` in `work_company` (index.php ~1312, ~1427), so the domain map starts as a small config array; move it to a table only when companies are managed in the UI. Confirmed by John: PMBSI = `pmbsi.com`, 2LOG = `2log.com` (only two companies exist for now).
- D11 **Every HR user sees every account password, including the Super Administrator account** (John overrode my exclusion: HR will manage that account too). Accepted risk, recorded in Decision-Log: any HR user can log in as the owner; the audit row per reveal is the only control. 
- D12 **Role clean-up is a SEPARATE later patch**: John wants to remove HR Leave, HR Timekeeping, Recruiter and Payroll because one HR account already has their access. Not in this patch, because it deletes roles and touches permissions (project rule: ask first). Today users on them: Recruiter 2, HR Leave 1, Payroll 2, HR Timekeeping 0 (Recruitment Manager 1 not mentioned, left alone). That patch must first compare permissions of each role against Human Resources, reassign those users in a migration with a guarded down script, then drop the roles. Until then the new dropdown only offers HR and Employee.

## Password storage (recommendation; D4 conflicts with BR-117)
Vault BR-117 says passwords are never reversible, and the UI says "cannot be revealed, even to a Super Administrator". D4 needs the opposite, so BR-117 gets a written exception plus a Decision-Log entry.
- Keep `password_hash` as today: login only checks the hash.
- Add an **encrypted copy** (openssl AES-256-GCM, random IV, key in git-ignored config outside the DB). Not plaintext, and not hash-only (a hash cannot be viewed).
- Rewrite the copy on every change (HR reset or employee change), so the eye always shows the current password.
- Every reveal: POST + CSRF + permission check + audit row (who, whose account, when; never the value). Masked until clicked.
- Accepted risk: HR/Super Admin can log in as any employee, and whoever gets the DB and the key sees every password. Mitigation: audit trail, key off the DB. Rollback = drop the one column, HR only resets.

## ASSUMPTIONS I'M MAKING (correct me now)
1. Same PHP app, MySQL `pmbsi_hris`, no framework; migrations in `database/migrations/` (next number 020).
2. Login id is `users.email` = generated `firstnamelastname@pmbsi.com` (D1): lowercase, spaces/accents/punctuation stripped, suffixes (Jr., III) dropped. Collisions: Q1.
3. Role for auto-created accounts is the existing Employee role. HR roles are still created elsewhere.
4. Generated password: 12 chars from `random_int`, mixed case + digits, no look-alike characters, meets the current 10-char/letter+number policy.
5. First login forces a password change (`must_change_password`; I did not find this column in code or migrations, so it may need a migration; to verify).
6. Existing 20 users stay untouched (D3). No bulk creation for existing employees without accounts (Q3).
7. Employee creation and account creation happen in one DB transaction; if either fails, neither is saved.

## Tech Stack
PHP 8, MySQL (XAMPP), plain PHP views in `index.php` and `app/*`, tests are plain PHP scripts run by `scripts/check.php`. `password_hash(PASSWORD_DEFAULT)` for login. New dependency: none (`openssl` is enabled; `sodium` is not).

## Code Style
Follow existing static-repository style: `public static function`, PDO prepared statements, `Auth::can()` checks, `csrf_field()`, `e()` escaping, audit via the existing audit helper.
```php
public static function issue(int $employeeId, string $email): array {
    $plain = self::generatePassword();               // random_int based
    $uid = FoundationRepository::createUser($name, $email, $plain, $employeeRoleId);
    self::storeIssued($uid, $plain);                 // encrypted, wiped on change
    Audit::log('user.auto_created', ['user_id'=>$uid,'employee_id'=>$employeeId]); // never log $plain
    return ['user_id'=>$uid];
}
```
UI text is English only.

## Testing Strategy
Plain PHP tests registered in `scripts/check.php` (floor raised in CONSTRAINTS.md, never lowered). Written first (red), then green.
- Unit: generator meets policy and is not repeated across 1000 runs; encrypt/decrypt round trip; copy rewritten on change; email generator (accents, spaces, suffixes, collisions).
- Integration (scratch DB only): create employee -> user exists, role Employee, linked, `must_change_password=1`, one transaction (force failure -> no employee, no user); duplicate email rejected; employee changes password -> HR eye shows the new value; login works with the generated password.
- Authorization: only users with the HR/Super Admin permission can reveal; reveal is POST + CSRF, audited, rate limited; employees cannot reveal anyone's.
- Static: "Link later" and Create New User form gone; `create_user` handler removed.
- Ticket: employee can file the forgotten-password ticket; HR resolves it via reset.
- Not run without John's word: browser checks; apply to `pmbsi_hris` follows the standing "test then apply" rule.

## Boundaries
- Always: validate and CSRF every POST; hash for login; audit account creation, reveal and reset (without the password value); run `check.php task`; vault sync; backup + isolated DB before migration.
- Ask first: any new column/table beyond the encrypted-copy column, new ticket category/permission, bulk-creating accounts for existing employees, changing which roles get an auto account.
- Never: log, email or put the password in a URL/query string/audit row; commit the encryption key; weaken or delete a test or floor; push/deploy; delete data or roles; show passwords to employees other than the owner flow.

## Success Criteria
1. Creating an employee yields exactly one linked, active Employee user, atomically.
2. HR sees the current password via the eye anytime (D4), audit row per reveal, nothing logged in plaintext; DB holds hash + encrypted copy only.
3. First login forces a change; after a change the eye shows the new password.
4. Forgotten-password request under HR Requests (D5) reaches HR, who can view or reset it.
5. "Link later" field and Create New User form are gone; no dead handler left.
6. `php scripts/check.php task` OK, floor raised, existing 20 users unchanged (row counts and hashes verified).
